full_text_en:
**Li Fuyong, Liu Jianxin, Yang Wengao — Sabotaging Electrical Power Equipment Case**

**Defendants:**

Defendant: Li Fuyong, male, 32 years old, peasant, from Kongzhongwang Village, Monan Township, Xian County, Hebei Province. On July 21, 1984, he absconded when an arrest warrant was issued for sabotaging electrical power equipment. He was arrested on June 29, 1985, again for sabotaging electrical power equipment.

Defendant: Liu Jianxin, male, 23 years old, peasant, from Kongzhongwang Village, Monan Township, Xian County, Hebei Province. Arrested on June 29, 1985.

Defendant: Yang Wengao, male, 38 years old, peasant, from Kongzhongwang Village, Monan Township, Xian County, Hebei Province. Arrested on June 29, 1985.

Defendant: Song Rushe, male, 33 years old, peasant, from Xilingxiao Village, Xicun Township, Shen County, Hebei Province. Arrested on June 29, 1985.

From the spring of 1983 to April 1985, defendant Li Fuyong, in collusion with defendant Liu Jianxin, went to nine villages including Hefang and Dongzhaoshi in Raoyang County, cutting and stealing 1,920 meters of 10,000-volt transmission lines and 24,075 meters of low-voltage transmission lines. Li Fuyong, in collusion with defendant Yang Wengao, went to six villages including Xiaohe and Qinzhongwang in Xian County and Weilou Village in Suning County, cutting and stealing 8,210 meters of low-voltage transmission lines, and dismantling and stealing 24 electricity meters and 9 mutual inductors from eleven villages in Suning and Xian counties. Li Fuyong, in collusion with Luo Tongxiu (dealt with in a separate case), cut and stole 1,260 meters of low-voltage transmission lines in Yechang Village, Xian County, and cut and stole 4,080 meters of low-voltage transmission lines from three villages — Dongduan, Xiaoju, and Yechang — in Xian County. Li Fuyong also, in collusion with Zhao Shuanzhu (dealt with in a separate case), cut and stole 2,340 meters of low-voltage transmission lines in Lisanjiaoluzhuang Village, Xian County.

From January to April 1985, defendant Liu Jianxin, in addition to jointly cutting and stealing a total of 25,995 meters of high- and low-voltage transmission lines with defendant Li Fuyong, also alone cut and stole 3,180 meters of low-voltage transmission lines from Nanshiqin Village and Hewo Village in Raoyang County.

Defendant Song Rushe, knowing that the transmission lines sold by defendants Li Fuyong, Liu Jianxin, and Yang Wengao were stolen by cutting, purchased over 30,000 meters, instructed his father and younger brother to sell them, and illegally profited.

Defendants Li Fuyong, Liu Jianxin, Yang Wengao, and others committed a total of 48 offenses, cutting and stealing over 45,000 meters of transmission lines valued at RMB 16,051 (including 1,920 meters of 10,000-volt high-voltage lines). This caused 101 motor-pumped wells in 32 villages in Xian, Suning, and Raoyang counties to be unable to irrigate fields, resulted in severe reduction of crop yields on over 5,900 mu of farmland, and caused great difficulties for the masses in water supply, lighting, and flour milling.

On September 7, 1985, the Hengshui Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province heard the case and determined: Defendant Li Fuyong successively committed 35 offenses, sabotaging transmission lines and other electrical power equipment, endangering public safety, causing severe damage to the production and people's livelihood in the affected villages. The circumstances were particularly flagrant and the consequences were especially serious, warranting severe punishment. Defendant Liu Jianxin successively committed 23 offenses in multiple locations, sabotaging transmission lines, with serious circumstances, warranting severe punishment. Defendant Yang Wengao participated in sabotaging electrical power facilities in 19 offenses and should also be punished. The acts of the above three defendants all constituted the crime of sabotaging electrical power equipment under Article 110 of the Criminal Law of the PRC. Defendant Song Rushe, knowing that the transmission lines sold by defendants Li Fuyong, Liu Jianxin, and Yang Wengao were stolen by cutting, engaged in the disposal of stolen goods, thereby constituting the crime of disposing of stolen goods. To safeguard public safety and social order, and to protect people's property from infringement, the court sentenced defendant Li Fuyong to death for the crime of sabotaging electrical power equipment, and, pursuant to Article 53, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, deprived him of political rights for life. It sentenced defendant Liu Jianxin to death, with a two-year reprieve, and, pursuant to Article 53, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, deprived him of political rights for life. It sentenced defendant Yang Wengao to fixed-term imprisonment of 12 years for the crime of sabotaging electrical power equipment, and, pursuant to Article 52 of the Criminal Law, deprived him of political rights for five years. It sentenced defendant Song Rushe to fixed-term imprisonment of 3 years for the crime of disposing of stolen goods.

After the judgment was pronounced, defendant Li Fuyong appealed to the Hebei High People's Court, claiming that cutting and stealing transmission lines was not intentional sabotage and that the sentence was too severe.

On October 28, 1985, the Hebei High People's Court, pursuant to Article 134, paragraph 2 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the PRC, reviewed the entire case and determined: The appellant Li Fuyong's sabotage of electrical power equipment was of long duration, involved many incidents and large quantities, and caused particularly serious consequences. Moreover, when an arrest warrant was issued for sabotaging electrical power equipment in 1984, he fled and continued committing offenses thereafter. A heavier punishment should be imposed. Li Fuyong, living in rural areas, was aware of the properties of high- and low-voltage transmission lines and electricity meters used in the countryside, and was also aware of the consequences of cutting transmission lines and dismantling electricity meters. His defense that cutting transmission lines was not intentional sabotage was untenable. The original judgment had clear findings of fact, conclusive evidence, accurate characterization of the crime, appropriate sentencing, and lawful procedures. Pursuant to Article 136, item (1) of the Criminal Procedure Law, the court ruled to reject Li Fuyong's appeal and affirm the original judgment.

The Hebei High People's Court, pursuant to the provisions of the Supreme People's Court authorizing High People's Courts to approve certain death sentences and Article 146 of the Criminal Procedure Law, approved the sentence of death for Li Fuyong to be carried out immediately, with deprivation of political rights for life, and approved the sentence of death with a two-year reprieve for Liu Jianxin, with deprivation of political rights for life.

The Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, at its 237th meeting on November 29, 1985, pursuant to Article 11, paragraph 1 of the Organic Law of the People's Courts of the PRC, concluded in summarizing trial experience that the crime of sabotaging electrical power equipment is a serious crime currently endangering public security and socialist modernization, and must be punished severely and swiftly according to law. The Hebei High People's Court and the Hengshui Intermediate People's Court were entirely correct in imposing severe punishment on criminals such as Li Fuyong and Liu Jianxin in accordance with the law.
